Calculate a self-organising map from EEM data

Source: R/som_functions.R
eemsom.Rd

The EEMs are unfolded into vectors (see eem2mat), normalised and arranged on a self-organising map (SOM, Kohonen 2013). Each unit of the map gets a prototype EEM (codebook vector). Similar samples are mapped to the same or neighbouring units. The calculation is done with som, please see details there.

Usage

eemsom(
  eem_list,
  dim = "auto",
  topo = "hexagonal",
  normalise = "sd",
  na = "remove",
  rlen = 500,
  alpha = c(0.05, 0.01),
  mode = "online",
  init = "pca",
  seed = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'eemsom'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

eem_list

object of class eemlist. All EEMs need to have the same excitation and emission wavelengths and unique sample names.

dim

size of the map, either "auto" (default) or a numeric vector c(xdim, ydim) with the number of columns and rows of units

topo

topology of the map, "hexagonal" (default) or "rectangular"

normalise

normalisation of each sample, see eem2mat

na

handling of missing values, see eem2mat

rlen

number of times the complete data set is presented to the map during training

alpha

learning rate, vector of start and end value

mode

training algorithm: "online" (default), "batch" or "pbatch" (parallel batch)

init

initialisation of the codebook vectors: "pca" (default) places them on the plane of the first two principal components, "random" uses randomly selected samples

seed

seed for the random number generator. With NULL (default), the current random number stream of the session is used, so set.seed before the call gives reproducible results. With a number, the seed is set for this calculation only and the random number state of the session is restored afterwards.

cores

number of cores used with mode = "pbatch"

verbose

print infos

...

additional parameters that are passed on to som, e.g. radius. keep.data is always TRUE, because the data are needed by eemsom_samples and other functions.

x

object of class eemsom

Value

object of class eemsom, a list containing

  • som: object of class kohonen, see som

  • ex, em: excitation and emission wavelengths

  • keep: logical vector of the unfolded wavelength pairs used in the SOM

  • samples: sample names

  • normalise, norm_factors: normalisation method and factors

  • na: handling of missing values

  • clusters: cluster of each unit, NULL until the units are clustered

  • settings: arguments used for som, needed by eemsom_stability

Details

With dim = "auto", the number of units is \(5 \sqrt{n}\) (Vesanto and Alhoniemi 2000) but not more than the number of samples n. The ratio of the side lengths follows the two largest eigenvalues of the data (Bieroza et al. 2009, Ejarque-Gonzalez and Butturini 2014): like in the SOM Toolbox (Vesanto et al. 2000), it is the square root of the ratio of the eigenvalues, i.e. the ratio of the standard deviations along the first two principal components. Ratios above the square root of the number of units are replaced by 1 to avoid very elongated maps.

The default learning rate (0.05 to 0.01) and the default neighbourhood radius (decreasing from two thirds of all unit distances to zero) of som correspond to the settings of Ejarque-Gonzalez and Butturini (2014).

The squared Euclidean distance (dist.fcts = "sumofsquares") is always used. Otherwise, kohonen would switch to the Tanimoto distance for data between 0 and 1 with row sums of 1, which occurs with normalise = "sum". With na = "keep", distances are calculated from the available wavelength pairs of a sample and scaled up to the number of all wavelength pairs.

The initialisation with init = "pca" is deterministic. The order of samples in the online training is random, so please set seed or use set.seed before the call for reproducible results.

The training time grows with the numbers of samples, units and wavelength pairs. As a rough guide for one core, online training with rlen = 500 takes about a minute for 200 EEMs with 3000 wavelength pairs and several minutes for 1000 EEMs. mode = "pbatch" with cores > 1, a smaller rlen or a lower resolution of the EEMs (see eem_range and eem_exclude; Ejarque-Gonzalez and Butturini (2014) used 366 wavelength pairs) reduce the time. This matters for eemsom_stability, which repeats the training many times.

References

Kohonen, T. (2013). Essentials of the self-organizing map. Neural Networks 37, 52-65. doi:10.1016/j.neunet.2012.09.018

Vesanto, J., Alhoniemi, E. (2000). Clustering of the self-organizing map. IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks 11(3), 586-600. doi:10.1109/72.846731

Vesanto, J., Himberg, J., Alhoniemi, E., Parhankangas, J. (2000). SOM Toolbox for Matlab 5. Report A57, Helsinki University of Technology.

Bieroza, M., Baker, A., Bridgeman, J. (2009). Exploratory analysis of excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectra with self-organizing maps as a basis for determination of organic matter removal efficiency at water treatment works. Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences 114(G4), 2009JG000940. doi:10.1029/2009JG000940

Ejarque-Gonzalez, E., Butturini, A. (2014). Self-Organising Maps and Correlation Analysis as a Tool to Explore Patterns in Excitation-Emission Matrix Data Sets and to Discriminate Dissolved Organic Matter Fluorescence Components. PLoS ONE 9(6), e99618. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0099618

Wehrens, R., Kruisselbrink, J. (2018). Flexible Self-Organizing Maps in kohonen 3.0. Journal of Statistical Software 87(7), 1-18. doi:10.18637/jss.v087.i07

See also

som, eemsom_samples, eemsom_codes, eemsom_quality

Other self-organising maps: eem2mat(), eempf_som(), mat2eem()

Examples

data(eem_list)

som <- eemsom(eem_list, rlen = 100, seed = 42)
som
#> Self-organising map of 15 EEMs
#>  map: 3 x 5 hexagonal units
#>  wavelength pairs: 4554 of 4554 
#>  normalisation: sd 
#>  clusters: none 
eemsom_samples(som)
